content.text:
`/search` returns one result per persisted funder UUID. It combines canonical-name and alias candidates with `UNION`, selects the strongest alias, and keeps the canonical name as the displayed name. Canonical wins score ties; alias ties use bytewise alphabetical order. Separate UUIDs remain separate, including identical names. [funder.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/outbound/funder.rs:34)

Resolution and loading already determine which observations belong together, the canonical name, aliases, and persisted UUID. Loading upserts by `resolution_identity_id`; search does no further identity resolution. [declaration_loading.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_loading.rs:403), [persistence](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_loading.rs:585)

The smallest snapshot regression case needs a query, strictness, expected canonical UUID/name, and expected alias provenance. Assert:

- HTTP 200.
- Expected `(kind, id)` occurs exactly once.
- Its `name`, `funder_kind`, and `match_source` equal expected values.
- If testing a known incorrect merge, assert the two expected IDs both remain present.

Avoid requiring the entire response or its ordering unless that is the regression. `max_entries` caps each entity type independently. The response is `{"entities":[...]}`; provenance is `{"kind":"name"}` or `{"kind":"alias","name":"..."}`. [handlers.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/inbound/http/handlers.rs:21)

Existing test coverage already sends real HTTP requests and proves two matching aliases produce one canonical result; it uses a newly created SQLx test database, not `exposed_search_regression`. [integration.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/tests/integration.rs:24), [HTTP helper](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/tests/common/mod.rs:29)

Launch against the existing snapshot from the repository root:

```sh
DATABASE_URL='REDACTED' \
cargo run --package exposed --bin exposed -- server
```

Use the port printed at startup; 6999 falls back to an available port if occupied. [server.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/inbound/http/server.rs:15)

```sh
curl --fail-with-body --get 'http://127.0.0.1:6999/search' \
  --data-urlencode 'term=EXAMPLE' \
  --data-urlencode 'strictness=1' \
  --data-urlencode 'max_entries=255'
```

These are source-derived commands; I did not launch the server or inspect snapshot contents. No database refresh is needed to test the existing snapshot.
